claim: In the matching retail DLL, instance WeaponMan.DeleteWeapon(Int32 idx) (0x06006AC6) has raw MethodDef row 94534300000086004dcf0a009f490000ab4d, RVA 0x00435394, signature blob 20010108, and an exact 57-byte fat-header body SHA-256 8855138052c3fa6baf7847766f20a3ff5ded2a517364b594dc4a7af747239be1. Its exact body returns for signed idx < 0, continues only for signed idx < 8, loads WeaponObj[idx], returns if UnityEngine.Object.op_Implicit is false, otherwise obtains the GameObject, calls UnityEngine.Object.DestroyObject, writes null back to WeaponObj[idx], and returns. Exact matching-DLL scanning finds three direct references across three caller methods: Player.ProcessAttackHit_Normal, Weapon.Update_Equipped, and WeaponMan.DeleteAllWeapons.
